title: Sigma Notation and the Sum to Infinity
seo_title: Grade 12 Sigma Notation and Sum to Infinity Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
short_title: Sigma Notation and Sum to Infinity
standard_text: Sigma notation; sum to infinity of a convergent geometric series: S∞ = a/(1 − r) for −1 < r < 1.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 12 worksheets: sigma notation, the sum to infinity and convergence of geometric series. 100 questions with memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Σi=1n Tᵢ means add T₁ + T₂ + … + Tₙ.
  • The number of terms from i = p to i = q is q − p + 1.
  • A geometric series converges only if −1 < r < 1. Then S∞ = a1 − r.
  • Find r by dividing a term by the term before it.

Examples

Example

8 + 4 + 2 + …

r = ½

Answer: S∞ = 8 ÷ ½ = 16

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting termsFrom 3 to 10 there are 8 terms.
|r| ≥ 1Then there is no sum to infinity.
1 + rS∞ = a ÷ (1 − r).

faq.a: Use sigma notation, and find the sum to infinity of a convergent geometric series: S∞ = a/(1 − r) for −1 < r < 1.
The sum gets closer and closer to one number.

items.q: A geometric series has common ratio r = x + 32. For which values of x does the series converge?
items.e: It converges when −1 < r < 1: −2 < x + 3 < 2, so −5 < x < −1.
